facts: The appeal was directed against the judgment and order dated April 16, 1976, of the Allahabad High Court confirming the conviction of the appellant under Section 302, Indian Penal Code and the sentence of death imposed on him thereunder for intentionally causing the death of his own son named Gorakh Prasad.
The story as put forth by prosecution was that the appellant who belongs to village Patra, District Gorakhpur was employed at the relevant time as Daftary in the D.A.V. College, Gorakhpur.

About a year and a half before the occurrence, the deceased who was a peon in the same institution gave up service at the instance of the appellant and set up a tea-stall in a portion of the shop of PW, Bharat Lal in form of the College.
The deceased used to accompany the appellant every evening to his village and to return to Gorakhpur next morning.
Some two months before the occurrence the appellant who was a widower started casting evil eyes on Kapoora and making indecent overtures to her.
issues: Whether the prosecution has established the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt?
petitioner_arguments: The appellant argued that the evidence against him was circumstantial and did not establish his guilt beyond reasonable doubt.
He also argued that there were inconsistencies in the testimony of the witnesses and that the prosecution had failed to prove its case.
respondent_arguments: The respondent/defending party argued that the evidence against the appellant was strong and established his guilt beyond reasonable doubt.
They also argued that the inconsistencies in the testimony of the witnesses were minor and did not affect the overall credibility of the prosecution's case.
court_reasoning: The court held that the evidence against the appellant was sufficient to establish his guilt beyond reasonable doubt.

It noted that the prosecution had presented a strong case and that the inconsistencies in the testimony of the witnesses were minor and did not affect the overall credibility of the prosecution's case.
holding: The court upheld the conviction and sentence of the appellant under Section 302, Indian Penal Code.
It held that the evidence against the appellant was sufficient to establish his guilt beyond reasonable doubt and that the sentence of death imposed on him was appropriate in the circumstances.
